summary: Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Hiroshi Tsuchiya, Hozan Saeki, Enryo Inoue, and Sarat Chandra Das, and held posts as Rector at Gohyaku Rakan-ji and Professor at Toyo University (1916).
Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).
Elaine Fisher works in Indology and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies at Columbia University (attested 2010) and became Assistant Professor at Stanford University in 2017.

Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Girton College, Cambridge, Oxford, and earned her PhD from the University of Warwick (1995), where she became Emeritus Professor around 1990.

Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under Roger Brown (1969), taught at Brown University, and was appointed Professor of Cognitive Psychology at UC Berkeley in 1971.

Elena Bashir specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan (graduated 1988) and later held posts at the University of Chicago, serving on an editorial board around 1998 and in a post in 2000.
Elena Beccarini-Crescenzi was an Indologist who studied at the University of Florence under Paolo Emilio Pavolini, graduating in 1915.
Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian History at Sapienza University of Rome under Luciano Petech (graduated 1971) and became an Associate Professor there in 1980.
Elena France Hanson is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who completed her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

Elena Mucciarelli works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Tübingen, where she was a researcher (2016–2017), before positions at Hebrew University and as Assistant Professor at the University of Groningen (2020).

Eli Franco (born 1953) is an Indologist and philosopher. After doctoral studies under Charles Malamoud and a habilitation at Hamburg, he held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and as Chair of Indology at Leipzig (2004–2021).

Elijah George Halhed Impey (1818–1868) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Bombay Medical Service, as Surgeon-Major in the Bombay Army (~1840–1864), and as Postmaster-General of the Bombay Presidency (1856–1868).

Elijah Sacvan Ary (born 1972) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University, completing his PhD under Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp in 2007.

Elimar Benda (1890–1976) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned a Dr.iur. at Jena (1913), attended Marburg, and held library posts at Humboldt University (1921–1922), University of Freiburg (1926–1936), and Heidelberg University (1936–1940).

Elimar Max Grube (1851–1891) was a scholar of Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and completed his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber (1874–1875).

Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a philosopher and Indologist. After completing his PhD at Columbia University (1960), he taught at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and served as Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006).

Elisa Freschi (born 1977) works in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Raffaele Torella, held posts at Sapienza University of Rome, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Vienna, and became Associate Professor at the University of Toronto (~2020).
Elisa Ganser is an Indologist who worked as an SNF project collaborator at the University of Zurich in 2018 and is attested as a lecturer at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Elisabeth Kreyenborg (born 1897) was an Indologist who earned her PhD at the University of Münster under Richard Schmidt (1930) and worked as a librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft from 1943 to 1950.
